newOrchestratorDirectAudit.finding: The new live contract-analysis orchestrator and its AnalysisRun model touch exactly three Prisma models (AnalysisRun, Document, ClaimReviewItem) and none of them are DebtEvent or LedgerEntry, directly or via a relation. Confirmed directly in prisma/schema.prisma: model AnalysisRun has fields id/companyId/packageKey/documentIds/analysisAlgorithmVersion/status/currentStage/startedAt/completedAt/fatalError/reviewItemCount/createdAt/updatedAt and a single relation to Company - no field or relation referencing Facility, DebtEvent, or LedgerEntry in any form. This is exactly as expected: contract-model/analysis is about covenant/definition/rule truth extracted from documents, not the financial ledger, and the schema confirms it has no coupling point to the financial-core-db tables at all.

conclusion.reasoning: Every fact the prior workstream's decision rested on is independently reconfirmed against the current HEAD (4005687), which includes all of Phase 3F.1.6.R's own new work (Workstream F's live contract-analysis orchestrator and its onboarding-actions integration): (1) the only three DebtEvent write call sites in the entire repository remain the same three offline, engineer-run, one-off scripts under scripts/ - no new call site exists anywhere in app/ or lib/, including nowhere in the new lib/contract-model/analysis/** package; (2) sourceLedgerEntryId remains written nowhere and read in exactly one place (lib/financial-core-db/adapter.ts, with the same `?? undefined` fallback); (3) the new AnalysisRun model and its orchestrator/service code touch only AnalysisRun, Document, and ClaimReviewItem - zero relation, zero field, zero runtime reference to DebtEvent or LedgerEntry, confirmed both by exhaustive grep (including a case-insensitive sweep for 'ledger'/'debtevent' across the entire analysis package, which returned nothing) and by direct reading of the five orchestrator source files and the AnalysisRun Prisma model definition; (4) docs/HEADROOM-ROADMAP.md, re-read directly rather than trusted from paraphrase, still explicitly and unambiguously assigns the LedgerEntry/DebtEvent reconciliation to Phase 6 - Living Headroom State, by name, in both its Phase 6 goal statement (line 111) and its dedicated §3.3/§5 fork discussion (line 178), with no contradicting or superseding language found anywhere else in the document. The two isolated comment-only 'DebtEvent'/'LedgerEntry' mentions found in lib/contract-model/ir/types.ts and lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic-precedent/types.ts are pre-existing design-rationale prose (present before this re-validation, unrelated to Workstream F's orchestrator) citing the roadmap's own fork discussion as a reason NOT to couple new IR/semantic-precedent schemas to the transitional LedgerEntry model - if anything, this is corroborating evidence that engineers building adjacent new schemas during this same phase are actively treating the fork as open, Phase-6-scoped architectural debt, not silently re-coupling to it. No fact underlying the prior decision has changed. The prior decision holds on independent re-inspection of the current code.
